units.title: Unit 1: The Present Perfect & Past Simple
units.description: Using present perfect for experiences and past simple for finished events with specific time references.

lessons.title: Distinguishing Present Perfect and Past Simple Tenses
lessons.summary: Understanding the usage of have/has + V3 versus past simple V2, with keywords like since, for, already, yet, and yesterday.
learningObjectives: Form sentences using have/has + past participle
Identify the difference between specific past time (in 2020, yesterday) and indefinite time
Correct common error patterns in Grade 9 English exams

sections.title: Grammar Rule & Comparison
sections.content: We use the Past Simple for actions completed at a specific time in the past (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2023). We use the Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) for actions that happened at an unspecified time or started in the past and continue to the present.
sections.formulaOrRule: Present Perfect: Subject + have/has + V3 (Past Participle)

keyRules: Past Simple needs a finished time word.
Present Perfect connects past and present.

faq.question: When do we use "since" vs "for"?
faq.answer: Use "since" with a specific starting point (since 2018, since Monday). Use "for" with a duration (for three years, for two hours).

examTips: Watch out for time markers in the exam sentence to choose the right tense form.
